passage:
Nancy was chosen to play a queen in the school play. She was excited until she saw the shoes. They were beautiful, but they were too large.
"You can still wear them," said her friend May. "Queens walk slowly anyway."
During practice, Nancy tried to walk like a queen, but the shoes kept slipping off. Everyone laughed, and Nancy wanted to quit.
That evening, her grandmother gave her a pair of plain black shoes. "A queen is not great because of her shoes," she said. "She is great because people believe her."
Nancy wore the black shoes at the play. They did not shine, but she could walk, turn, and stand tall. After the show, many people said she looked like a real queen.
May looked at the old shoes and said, "Maybe the best costume is the one that lets you act."
